chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who had an umm walad (concubine who bore him a child), and he married her to a man, and she bore him a boy. Then the man died, and she returned to her master. Is it permissible for him to have intercourse with her? He said: 'She observes the waiting period from the husband for four months and ten days, then he has intercourse with her by ownership (milk) without a new marriage contract.'

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine who bore her master a child
key_terms.اَلْمِلْكِ: Ownership (referring to possession of a concubine)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a master regarding his umm walad after she is married and her husband dies?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlighting the distinct juristic view that a master retains the right to consummate relations with his freed concubine through ownership (milk al-kan) rather than a new marriage contract (nikah) after her iddah from the second husband. This reflects the Shia position on the flexibility of marital bonds for concubines, distinguishing their status from free women where a new contract is typically required for remarriage to the former husband.
